A.explanation: $x$ is the maximum displacement from equilibrium and $y$ is the time for one complete oscillation, so amplitude and period.

B.explanation: Frequency is $1/T$ and is not a vertical distance on the graph, while $x$ measures the peak displacement.

C.explanation: $x$ is amplitude, but wavelength is a distance along the wave and cannot be read from a displacement-time axis.

D.explanation: Neither quantity is correct because a displacement-time graph shows period on the time axis, not wavelength, and frequency is not a graph distance.

hints: Look at the axes: $x$ is a vertical displacement to the crest and $y$ is a horizontal interval on the time axis.
Recall that amplitude is the maximum displacement from $0$ and the time for one full cycle of the particle is the period $T$.
Ask why wavelength cannot appear here: wavelength needs a displacement-distance graph, and frequency is calculated as $1/T$, not measured as a length.
walkthrough: Identify the graph type: vertical axis is displacement and horizontal axis is time for one particle in the progressive wave.
Interpret $x$: it runs from the equilibrium line at $0$ to the top of the crest, which is the definition of maximum displacement or amplitude.
Interpret $y$: it runs on the time axis from one point on the wave to the identical point one full oscillation later, covering one crest and one trough.
State the rule: time for one complete vibration is the period $T$, whereas wavelength $\lambda$ would require distance on the horizontal axis.
Conclude that $x$ = amplitude and $y$ = period. This is option A.
